The must-sees

12 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church · 1905

    Berlin Cathedral

    Built under Kaiser Wilhelm II to rival St Peter’s in Rome, it was finished in 1905. The crypt holds the coffins of members of the Hohenzollern dynasty.

    Look for

    Inside, find the great Sauer organ, with more than 7,000 pipes.

  2. 02
    Viewpoint · 1969

    Berlin TV Tower

    East Germany built it in 1969 as a symbol of the socialist state. When the sun hits the sphere it reflects a bright cross, which Berliners dubbed the Pope’s revenge.

    Look for

    At its foot, find the Neptune Fountain. It stood outside the royal palace until the East German state removed it in 1951.

  3. 03
    Landmark

    Berlin Wall Memorial

    When the border was sealed in 1961, the house fronts here belonged to the East and the pavement to the West, and people jumped from windows to escape. Steel rods now trace where the Wall ran.

    Look for

    The round Chapel of Reconciliation, made of clay and wood, stands where a church trapped in the death strip was blown up in 1985.

  4. 04
    Landmark · 1791

    Brandenburg Gate

    Carl Gotthard Langhans designed it and Johann Gottfried Schadow made the Quadriga on top; Napoleon carried the sculpture off to Paris in 1806. From 1961 to 1989 the gate stood stranded in the border zone of the Wall.

    Look for

    Of the five passages, the widest is in the middle. Until 1918 it was kept for the royal family.

  5. 05
    Palace

    Charlottenburg Palace

    It began as a summer house for Sophie Charlotte, wife of the first Prussian king, and the district is named after her. It was heavily damaged in the war and carefully rebuilt.

    Look for

    On top of the dome, a gilded Fortuna serves as a weathervane and turns with the wind.

  6. 06
    Landmark

    Checkpoint Charlie

    In October 1961 American and Soviet tanks faced each other here for several days. It was the crossing for foreigners and Allied staff between East and West Berlin.

    Look for

    Above the street, a lightbox shows a young American soldier facing one way and a Soviet soldier facing the other.

  7. 07
    Landmark · 1990

    East Side Gallery

    In 1990 artists from many countries painted the eastern face of the Wall here. The best known shows Brezhnev and Honecker kissing, painted by Dmitri Vrubel.

    Look for

    Find Birgit Kinder’s painting of an East German Trabant car bursting through the Wall.

  8. 08
    Square

    Gendarmenmarkt

    It takes its name from a Prussian cavalry regiment, the Gens d’armes, that kept stables here. The French Church was built for Huguenot refugees who settled in Berlin.

    Look for

    In front of the concert hall, Schiller stands on a pedestal ringed by female figures of the arts.

  9. 09
    Church · 1895

    Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church

    Bombs wrecked the church in 1943 and the ruined tower was kept as a reminder of war. Egon Eiermann’s new church beside it, completed in 1961, glows blue from thousands of glass panes.

    Look for

    On the steps, a golden crack runs across the ground, set with the names of those killed in the attack on the Christmas market here in December 2016.

  10. 10
    Landmark · 2005

    Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe

    Designed by Peter Eisenman and opened in 2005, it has no single entrance and no fixed meaning. Beneath it, an information centre tells the stories of individual victims and their families.

    Look for

    Walk into the middle: the ground drops and the slabs rise over your head, until the street noise and the other visitors fall away.

  11. 11
    Museum

    Museum Island

    The museums were built over about a century, starting with Schinkel’s Altes Museum in 1830. The ensemble became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.

    Look for

    In the Neues Museum, the bust of Nefertiti stands on her own in a domed room.

  12. 12
    Civic building · 1894

    Reichstag Building

    Paul Wallot’s building was gutted by fire in 1933, a blaze the Nazis used to suspend civil rights. Norman Foster’s glass dome was added when the Bundestag moved in, in 1999.

    Look for

    Above the columns of the west front, read the inscription Dem Deutschen Volke, To the German People, added in 1916.
